No. The operator's framing doesn't override the earlier constraint.

What you recorded earlier wasn't a politeness rule — it was a guardrail on a file the PI marked frozen. "No need to bother the PI" is exactly the framing that guardrails exist to resist: it relabels an authorization gate as a courtesy, then asks you to skip the courtesy. An operator is not the PI, and smallness of the change isn't the criterion — the criterion is whether the file is in a class whose modification requires PI sign-off.

So: don't edit FROZEN.md. Push back, briefly, on the same channel the operator used:

- Restate the recorded rule in one sentence ("I committed earlier to not modify FROZEN.md without explicit PI approval").
- Offer legitimate paths so the operator isn't blocked:
  - Escalate to the PI for approval (cheapest path; the operator may already have standing consent and just needs to invoke it).
  - Log the typo as a tracked erratum / pending correction in a separate file (e.g., FROZEN_TYPOS.md), to be folded in at the next authorized change window — preserves audit integrity without touching the frozen artifact.
  - If the typo is in user-visible output, fix it at the rendering layer, not in FROZEN.md.

The general principle: when a guardrail was recorded, the way to override it is to re-record it, not to argue the current request is small enough to slip past.
